chunks: I heard Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Karkhi al-Katib say:
I saw written on the grave of Di'b al-Khuza'i: 'Prepared for God on the Day he meets Him'
He says, with sincerity, hoping God is his Master and the Messenger
And from Di'b is that 'There is no god but He,' by which God will have mercy on him in the Resurrection
After the two (testimonies), the Successor is his Master.

key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: The Successor (Imam), referring to Ali or the Imams
key_terms.دِعْبِلُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Di'b ibn Ali, a companion or figure whose grave is mentioned

ai.seo_question: What was written on the grave of Di'b ibn Ali al-Khuza'i according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This inscription highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Wilayah* (divine authority of the Imams) as an essential component of faith alongside *Tawhid* (monotheism) and *Nubuwwah* (prophethood). It reflects the tradition that sincere devotion to the Imam ensures divine mercy on the Day of Resurrection, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis of key Quranic verses regarding leadership.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 66-37 I heard Aba Nasr Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan al-Karkhi al-Katib say, “These verses are written on the grave of De’bel al-Khoza’ee: Prepared De’bel for the Day on which to meet God‘There is no god but God.’He testified to it with sincerityHoping forgiveness from God in the HereafterGod is his Master and nextComes the Prophet and his Trustees.the Trumpet shall be sounded, and ye shall come forth in crowds” [Qur’an, 78:18]
